  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that Torah, charity, and prayer are the three pillars upon which the world stands, and since the world was created for Israel and Torah, these pillars existed from the very beginning of creation.</sectionSummaryBrief>

    <t s="7">And since the existence and standing of the world is upon these three pillars,</t>

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces two interpretations of the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace": the simple meaning that Hashem redeems the righteous, and the Sages' interpretation that man redeems Hashem, so to speak, through Torah, charity, and communal prayer.

translations.translation: Now, in this verse there are two interpretations.
The simple interpretation of "He redeemed my soul in peace" is that the Holy One, blessed be He, redeems the righteous
[both according to the simple meaning of the matter, which refers to the redemption of Dovid,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, redeemed him from the wars that came upon him,
and as it is brought in the Yerushalmi
that "He redeemed my soul in peace" refers to the redemption of Dovid from the war of Avshalom,
and so too regarding the "He redeemed my soul in peace" of the redemptions of Yud-Tes Kislev, Yud Kislev, and Yud-Beis Tammuz,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, redeemed the righteous],
and the second interpretation is as our Sages, of blessed memory, said:
The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Whoever engages in Torah, acts of kindness, and prays with the congregation, etc., it is as if he redeemed Me, etc.,
that man
(who engages in Torah, etc.)
redeems the Holy One, blessed be He, as it were.
And one must understand the connection between these two interpretations,
for in addition to the known fact that all interpretations of a single verse are related to each other,
behold, in the discourses of Yud-Tes Kislev
and Yud-Beis Tammuz
(when the matter of "He redeemed my soul in peace" occurred in its simple sense,
as above)
it is brought
(in many of them)
at their beginning and start, the aforementioned teaching of our Sages,
behold this emphasizes even more that these two interpretations are related to each other.
And one must understand the connection between the two interpretations.
And even though according to the aforementioned teaching of our Sages, the verse also speaks
(also)
about the matter of the redemption of Israel,
"He redeemed me, me and my children"
[And in the Chiddushei Aggados of the Maharsha
there, that the Shechinah said "He redeemed my soul in peace" with "those close to me," meaning my children],
behold this is regarding the one being redeemed,
but regarding the redeemer,
behold according to the simple interpretation,
"He redeemed," etc., refers to the Holy One, blessed be He,
and according to the aforementioned teaching of our Sages,
"He redeemed," etc., refers to the man who engages in Torah, etc.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Torah, charity, and prayer are the three pillars upon which the world stands, and since the world was created for Israel and Torah, these pillars existed from the very beginning of creation.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing that the three matters of Torah, charity, and prayer
(in a congregation),
through which "He redeemed me, me and my children,"
are the three pillars upon which the world stands
(as stated in the Chiddushei Aggados of the Maharsha there
and likewise in the Rashba there).
And since the existence and standing of the world is upon these three pillars,
it must be said
that these three matters also existed at the beginning of creation.
And even though it is known that the creation of the world was from the aspect of "for
He desires kindness"
(and only now does it depend on an arousal from below),
nevertheless,
since the purpose of creation from the outset is for the sake of Israel and for the sake of the Torah,
it must be said
that these three matters are the pillars of the world even at the beginning of its coming into being.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that through the foreknowledge of Israel's future service, the form of the three pillars was engraved in the Divine thought before creation, enabling the world to come into being.

translations.translation: And the explanation is,
behold, the teaching of the Maggid of Mezeritch is known
and the teaching of our master, the Alter Rebbe
[which is called
(also)
by his name]
on the statement of our Sages, of blessed memory,
"Know what is above from you,"
that everything that is above is all from you.
And from the continuation of the matter there, it is understood
that through the service of man, the matter above is effected even before the service.
And as the Maggid of Mezeritch said
on the verse
"Let us make man in our image," etc.,
that it is like the parable of a man who has a son,
that from the greatness of his love for him,
the form of the son is engraved in his thought.
And since with Him, blessed be He, the past and the future are one,
therefore the form of Israel was engraved
(as the souls of Israel are in the aspect of created beings,
and more than that, as they descend below)
in His thought, blessed be He, even before they were created.
For this is also the matter of "He took counsel with the souls of the righteous,"
that what was known before Him, blessed be He, that He would delight, as it were, in the service of the righteous,
behold this delight arose before Him, blessed be He, even before creation
(and through this, creation came about).
And this is what the three pillars
(Torah, service, and charity)
were also at the beginning of creation,
for since the Holy One, blessed be He, contracted Himself into the form of Israel
(even before they were created),
behold, through the service of Israel of Torah, service, and charity,
which are the three lines of Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferes
(and the three matters of thought, speech, and action),
there is effected above
(even before creation)
the form of Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferes
(and of thought, speech, and action),
and all the worlds come into being.
